newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope well, to appear in public on Sunday - Vatican.
newsitem.headline: Pope well, to appear in public on Sunday - Vatican.

text.p: Pope John Paul, laid low by an influenza which has forced him to cancel audiences, is well and will make his next public appearance on Sunday, the Vatican said on Friday.
"The Pope's next public appointment will be Sunday's Angelus," spokesman Joaquin Navarro-Valls said, referring to the weekly address the Pope makes from his window overlooking St Peter's Square.
"Therefore, that means that he is well," Navarro-Valls said.
The Polish-born Pope, 76, had been due to visit a Rome parish on Sunday morning before the Angelus address but that engagement has apparently been postponed.
It was not clear if the Pope, who has had a string of health problems in recent years, would be holding private audiences in the Vatican's Apostolic Palace before Sunday.
The leader of the world's 960 million Roman Catholics cancelled his general audience on Wednesday because of influenza and a sore throat. Doctors ordered him to stay in bed for a few days.
